details.description: CodeQwen1.5-7B is Alibaba Cloud's code-specialized language model built on the Qwen1.5 architecture, pretrained on about 3 trillion tokens of code data and supporting 92 programming languages with a 64K-token context window. It uses grouped-query attention for efficient inference. It is a base model for code completion, infilling and generation rather than conversation -- Qwen's own model card says 'we do not advise you to use it for chat' and recommends it instead for fine-tuning, code infilling, and code generation.
advantages: Scores 51.8% pass@1 on HumanEval and 72.2% pass@1 on MBPP (0-shot), per Qwen's CodeQwen1.5 announcement.
Also reports 45.7% pass@1 on HumanEval+ (0-shot), per Qwen's CodeQwen1.5 announcement.
Covers 92 programming languages; Qwen evaluated it on eight of them (Python, C++, Java, PHP, TypeScript, C#, Bash, JavaScript) via MultiPL-E.
disadvantages: Base model, not tuned for chat: Qwen's own model card advises against using it for chat and recommends fine-tuning, infilling, or generation instead.
Licensed under Alibaba's custom Tongyi Qianwen Research license rather than a fully permissive open-source license.
Requires transformers>=4.37.0; earlier versions raise a KeyError for its qwen2 architecture, per Qwen's model card.
use_cases: Code completion and infilling across 92 programming languages.
Base model for fine-tuning on downstream code-generation tasks.
Text-to-SQL and bug-fixing tasks, per Qwen's model card.

notes: Bud serves this model as 'chat' kind via /v1/chat/completions, but Qwen's own model card advises against using this base checkpoint for chat and recommends fine-tuning, infilling, or generation instead; kept Bud's routing/kind as given. The catalog's 65536-token input/output limits match Qwen's stated 64K context length. Found no dedicated public GitHub repository for this specific model, so github_url is left null.
